archetype.name: Fringe Contender (frontcourt-powered)
archetype.definition: A team with back-to-back 52-win seasons and an A+ frontcourt and wing group, good enough to be in the top tier on the site, still needing to show its defense can return to the level that made it a contender.

report.headline: A red-hot offense is covering for a defense that has lost its rim
report.take:
Houston opens 3-0 and fifth on the site, and the way it is winning is not the way it won the last two years. The 52-30 teams of 2024-25 and 2025-26 were built on defense, ranked 4th and 6th, with offenses ranked 13th and 8th. Three games in, it has flipped: the ORtg is 122.9, 3rd in the league, while the DRtg of 113.1 sits 17th. The Net Rtg of 9.8 (8th) is strong, but it is an offense number.

That offense is a frontcourt story. Kevin Durant has 72 points on a 71 TS %, Alperen Şengün has 69 points with a 28 USG % and 19 assists, and Jabari Smith Jr. is shooting a 67.2 TS %. Both the frontcourt and the wings, where Amen Thompson has 53 points and 31 rebounds, grade A+. The team TS % of 62.6 ranks 2nd and the 3P % of 41.7 ranks 4th, while the 3PA Rate of 37.6 is only 26th. That fits who they have been: a team that wins inside and on the offensive glass (ORB % 31.9, 8th) and now happens to be making the threes it does take. The backcourt is the soft spot at C+, with Marcus Smart out and Fred VanVleet orchestrating (16 assists) but scoring inefficiently at a 50.6 TS %.

The numbers flatter the defense more than the defense deserves. Opponents are hitting 29.3% from three, 5th lowest, which is mostly variance this early. Underneath, opponents are finishing 75.4% at the rim, 28th in the league and well above the 64.5 Houston allowed last season. It hasn't been leaking shots there, since the Opp Rim Rate of 26.3 ranks 6th, but what gets there goes in. Small forwards have hurt it too: 33 points a game to the position, ranked 28th. The record is also a bit ahead of the margin. After an 128-110 opener over Dallas came 114-110 at San Antonio and 121-114 at Atlanta, and the margin implies 2 wins, not 3.

Where this goes depends on the two numbers most likely to move. The three-point shooting, for and against, will come back toward the league, which costs some of the cushion. The rim defense should improve too, given its track record. If it does, this is the same 50-plus-win team as before, with a better offense. If it doesn't, Houston becomes a good offensive team with an ordinary defense, which is a lower ceiling than it has had.

strengths.title: Elite efficiency from the frontcourt
strengths.body: Durant, Şengün and Smith are combining volume and efficiency, and the frontcourt grades A+. Durant's 71 TS % will cool, but Şengün as the hub and Smith as a finisher are roles that should hold up. The offense ranking 3rd rests mostly on them.

strengths.title: Shot quality over shot volume
strengths.body: Houston takes relatively few threes but ranks near the top in every shooting-efficiency stat, and still crashes the offensive glass. The 3P % will regress, but the inside-out profile and offensive rebounding were there last season too, so the core of this offense is real.

strengths.title: Amen Thompson's two-way load
strengths.body: Thompson leads the wings in minutes and production, ranks 6th on the small forwards tab, and is a big reason the wings grade A+. His -47.3 On-Off is a three-game artifact of lineups and bench minutes, not a verdict on him.

concerns.title: Rim protection has collapsed
concerns.body: Opponents are finishing at 75.4% within four feet, 28th in the league and well above the league average, after Houston held them to 64.5 last season. Three games is a small sample, but this is the gap between a 17th-ranked defense and the top-six units of the last two years. Watch whether it closes.

concerns.title: Opponent three-point luck
concerns.body: Opponents are shooting 29.3% from three, well below the league. Defenses have little control over that over a season, so when it normalizes the DRtg will rise unless the rim defense improves.

concerns.title: Thin, shaky backcourt
concerns.body: The backcourt grades C+ with Smart out, and VanVleet's 50.6 TS % means the guards are setting up the bigs rather than scoring. Opposing small forwards are also feasting, a wing-defense hole that the guards and bench aren't covering.

trend.note: An 18-point-style blowout of Dallas at home, then two narrower road wins at San Antonio and Atlanta. The margin implies 2 wins, so the 3-0 is slightly ahead of the play, but three games is barely a trend.

weekAhead.headline: Five games, three soft defenses, and an OKC litmus test
weekAhead.body:
Houston gets Atlanta again at home, then goes to Milwaukee and Dallas before coming home for Oklahoma City and Boston. Milwaukee (0-3, DRtg 122, 26th) and Dallas (site rank 23, already beaten 128-110) are defenses this offense should carve, and Boston (site rank 22) rebounds poorly enough to give Houston extra possessions. That's three games to bank.

The harder two are Atlanta and OKC. The Hawks are 2-1 with a 15.4 Net Rtg, but they've been soft at the rim and torched by power forwards, which is Houston's strength. OKC comes in 3-0 with the league's 2nd-best DRtg and rim protection, on the second night of a back-to-back after Dallas. A 4-1 week is the reasonable target; anything less probably means the OKC game exposed the half-court offense against real resistance.

keyMatchups.title: Durant and Smith versus Atlanta's fours
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta has allowed 33.67 points a game to power forwards, 11.17 above those players' averages, the worst in the league, and its frontcourt grades D-. Opponents also finish 76.7% at the rim against them. Houston's power forwards should have a big night again.

keyMatchups.title: OKC's defense on a back-to-back
keyMatchups.body: The Thunder allow 97.2 per 100 possessions (2nd) and 55.1% at the rim (2nd), and force turnovers at the 2nd-highest rate. That's the opposite of the defenses Houston has been scoring against. Their own offense ranks 22nd, so Houston's leaky interior may matter less here than its ability to score.

keyMatchups.title: Şengün against Boston's glass
keyMatchups.body: Boston grabs just 45% of available rebounds (27th) and has allowed 26 points a game to centers (28th). Şengün and the offensive rebounders should get extra possessions and good looks inside.

weekAhead.watch: Opponents' rim finishing, especially against OKC and Atlanta: if it stays near 75%, the defense problem is real.

restOfSeason.body:
The frontcourt and wings make this a top-ten team, and the offensive profile of efficient shots and offensive rebounding should hold even as the 41.7% three-point shooting cools. I'd project an ORtg settling around 116 to 120, still a top-eight offense, rather than the current 122.9. The defense goes the other way: opponents won't keep shooting 29% from three, but a group that ranked 4th and 6th the last two years shouldn't keep allowing 75% at the rim either. I expect the DRtg to land around 111 to 115.

That adds up to a team in the 50 to 57 win range, similar to the last two seasons but with more offense. The upside depends on the defense returning to form; the downside is a backcourt that grades C+ and depends on Smart's health, and a frontcourt whose two stars are carrying an unsustainable shooting share.
swingFactors: Rim defense returning to last year's level
Marcus Smart's return and backcourt play

confidence.note: Three games: the shooting numbers on both ends are largely noise.
